seen_animation: Frames 1-6: a line-drawn pig in profile, facing left, stands still on a ground line under grey fence lines; a long straight line runs from the top-left corner down to its spiral snout, like a pole held to the nose. In frame 6 that line lies at a shallower angle. Frame 7: the pole line is gone, the head has dropped slightly and the chin stroke has bent into a hook. Frame 8: the whole pig is shifted right and lower, the head is larger and the body is cropped by the right edge. Frames 9-12: the pig moves back left and grows larger in frame; from frame 10 on, the back is drawn as one long straight line rising from the rear ear tip to a high, domed top, making the body taller than in frames 1-7, and the leg ticks reappear along the bottom. Frame 13: the head is at the lower-left corner, the largest it gets. Frames 14-16: the head moves back right to about one third across and holds there while the body fills the frame. The pig stays in strict side profile in all 16 frames.
seen_film: Frames 1-6: a white pig stands in side profile facing left in a pen in front of a chain-link fence, with a snare pole held to its snout from the upper left; a handler's legs are visible behind it. Frame 7: the pole comes off and the pig starts to step forward and turn its head toward the camera. Frame 8: the pig has turned to a three-quarter view facing the camera, head at about one third across. Frames 9-12: the pig walks toward the camera and down-left, growing larger, in three-quarter front view. Frame 13: the pig is closest, its head at the lower-left. Frames 14-16: the camera reframes and the head sits center-left, facing the camera, while the pig keeps walking slowly.
evidence: Frames 1-6 match the film well: profile pose, pole line to the snout at the same angle and place, pole angle flattening at 6. Frame 7 removes the pole at the same moment as the film. Head positions and growth in 8-16 track the film (head at lower-left in 13, back to center-left in 14-16). But the film's main turn of events, the pig turning its head from profile to face the camera between frames 7 and 8, is not performed: frames 8-16 keep the head in the same side profile with both ears on top and the snout pointing left. Motion also pops: from 7 to 8 the pig jumps right and down with the chin redrawn; from 8 to 9 it jumps back left and the back line and legs are redrawn in a different arrangement; from 10 to 11 the body suddenly gets taller with a steep straight back line; from 12 to 13 the head drops far to the lower-left in one step (the film also moves here, but the animation's body shape changes at the same time).
primary_gap: The pig never turns its head toward the camera after the pole is released, so the animation shows a profile pig sliding and growing instead of the film's pig turning and walking toward the viewer.
closes_when: Between frames 7 and 9 the snout spiral moves to sit below and between the two ear zigzags (ears splitting to either side of the head) and stays in that front-facing arrangement through frame 16, with the body changing by small steps each frame.
protect: The exact doodle construction in frames 1-7 (zigzag double-peak ears, spiral boxed snout, open separate chest stroke, short tick legs, rear double stroke); the pole line to the snout in frames 1-6 and its removal at frame 7; the film-matched framing and scale growth in 8-16, including the head reaching the lower-left at 13; the sparse grey fence and ground lines.
identity_gap: From frame 10 on the back is redrawn as a long straight line from the rear ear tip to a tall dome, which makes the body boxier and taller than the long low oval of c.png, though the ears, snout and legs remain the doodle's own strokes.
